questions.stem: In which architecture is the Serving Layer the last component?
questions.explanation: The Serving Layer is the last component of the Lambda Architecture, the layer exposed to end users for reporting.

questions.stem: To whom is the Serving Layer exposed, and for what purpose?
options: To source systems, for data ingestion
To end users, for reporting purposes
questions.explanation: The Serving Layer is the last layer, exposed to end users for reporting purposes.

questions.stem: Which kind of system is NOT meant to be exposed for reporting purposes?
questions.explanation: OLTP systems are not meant to be exposed for reporting; the Serving Layer uses stores such as a Data Warehouse, OLAP, Data Lake, NoSQL or Semantic Layer instead.

questions.stem: Which layer should ideally be treated as the Serving Layer when it is designed for a specific business requirement?
questions.explanation: If the Serving Layer is designed for a specific business requirement, the Semantic Layer is the last layer and should be treated as the Serving Layer.

questions.stem: If a Serving Layer is designed for generic use, which stores can fulfil that role?
options: Data Warehouse, OLAP, Data Lake or NoSQL
questions.explanation: For generic use, the Serving Layer can be a Data Warehouse, OLAP, Data Lake, NoSQL and so on.

questions.stem: Why is the JDBC Connector described as the most generic way to connect to any system?
options: Because every system has at least Java
Because it is the fastest connector
Because it is free of security parameters
Because it only works with OLAP
questions.explanation: Since every system has at least Java, JDBC is the most generic way to connect, using the other system's host name, IP, username and password.

questions.stem: How does a Native Driver differ from a plain JDBC or ODBC connector?
options: It does not use JDBC or ODBC at all
It is used only for online portals
It is built on JDBC and ODBC connectors but can also include security parameters
questions.explanation: Native drivers are internal drivers built with JDBC and ODBC connectors; the difference is that they can also include security parameters.

questions.stem: What is the major difference between Native Drivers and APIs for connecting to the Serving Layer?
options: Native Drivers connect source and target databases, whereas APIs expose data on online portals
APIs do not use JDBC or ODBC
Native Drivers are slower than APIs
Native Drivers are only for NoSQL
questions.explanation: Both are built on JDBC and ODBC with security parameters; Native Drivers connect databases from source to target, while APIs expose data on online portals.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a technology for connecting to the Serving Layer?
questions.explanation: JDBC, ODBC, Native Driver and API are the listed connection technologies; a floppy drive is not.

questions.stem: Which vendor is named as supporting the ODBC connector?
questions.explanation: ODBC is described as supported by Oracle and recently available on most systems.
